description: Ex-Congolese airliner, construction number 19195. One of three airframes withdrawn at N'Djili, cut up, trucked east to the Nsele valley and reassembled on a landscaped hilltop in the park, where the three between them house a restaurant, a nightclub and a VIP lounge. spottingmode.com codes all three preserved. Esri WorldView-2 imagery of 3 June 2022 shows three complete airliners standing on made-up pads served by a loop access road, paved walkways and an adjacent building - a deliberate installation, not a dump. Which of the three carries which function is not separately sourced, so the fit-out is not attributed to individual airframes.
museum_name: Parc de la Vallée de la N'Sele

description: Ex-Congolese airliner, construction number 20795. Second of the three airframes moved from N'Djili to the park and rebuilt on the hilltop display. Identified in the 2022 satellite image as the narrow-body with a conventional fin standing north-east of the TriStar.
museum_name: Parc de la Vallée de la N'Sele

description: Construction number 1209, previously with Air Canada and Delta Air Lines, latterly Hewa Bora Airways. Stored at N'Djili from 2007, then cut into three sections, moved to the park and reassembled on the hilltop. Reported by aviation24.be in September 2019 as the centrepiece of a scheme to convert three aircraft into a bar-disco, a restaurant and a hotel. The largest airframe visible in the 2022 imagery, on a paved pad with an awning structure alongside.
museum_name: Parc de la Vallée de la N'Sele
